About Holzbaurechner

Free calculators for timber projects, so that while you are still planning you know how much timber you need and roughly what it costs.

Who is behind it

Holzbaurechner (German for “timber construction calculator”) is run by Theo-Phil Penner from Innsbruck, Austria. I am a master mason and know the questions that come up before every building project: which sections do I need, how many beams and boards, and what will the timber cost? The calculators answer exactly these questions, quickly and without signing up.

How the calculators work

Each calculator starts from a proven basic design, for example a carport with posts, beams and rafters, or a raised bed with horizontal boards and corner posts. From your sizes the calculator works out the individual parts: section, length and quantity. That gives the volume of timber in cubic metres, and with the price per m³ and a waste allowance, the cost estimate.

How each design is built is explained on every calculator page, right below the calculator. That way you can see what the calculation is based on and compare the result with your own plan.

The sections are continental standard sizes and are shown in millimetres. Stock sizes in the UK, Ireland and Australia can differ slightly. If your merchant does not stock a size, choose the next size up.

Where the timber prices come from

The prices on the English pages are example retail prices per cubic metre for the UK and Ireland (including VAT) and for Australia (including GST). The calculators pick the currency from your location, and you can switch it under every calculator. Timber prices vary by region, merchant, grade and quantity. That is why you can enter your own price in every calculator, for example from your merchant's quote.

Where the limits are

The sections are guide values for planning and buying timber. They do not replace a structural calculation. For carports and patio covers in particular, the sections you need depend on snow load, wind load and span at your site. Whether you need planning permission or building regulations approval depends on where you live, so check with your local council.

Free and without signing up

All calculators are free. The website is funded by advertising and affiliate links. Below some calculators there are links to Amazon marked “paid link”. If you buy through one, you pay the same price and I earn a small commission. Neither ads nor commissions influence the results; the cutting list names no brands and no merchants. What you enter stays in your browser and is not stored. Details are in the privacy policy.

Found a mistake or missing a project?

If you notice a calculation error or would like a calculator for another project, please get in touch. You will find all the ways to reach me on the contact page.
